questions.question: Which of the following is considered a defining feature of living organisms without any exception?
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the defining feature because all living organisms show metabolism, and no non-living object exhibits it.

questions.question: Consciousness is defined as awareness of surrounding environments. Which organism possesses 'self-consciousness'?
questions.explanation: Self-consciousness is the awareness of oneself and is a characteristic of human beings only.

questions.question: According to binomial nomenclature, scientific names are written in which language and script?
options: Latin and printed in plain text
English and printed in plain text
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature requires scientific names to be written in Latin and printed in italics.

questions.question: In the scientific name Mangifera indica Linn., what does 'Linn.' indicate?
questions.explanation: 'Linn.' is an abbreviation for Linnaeus, who was the first to describe this species.

questions.question: Which taxonomic category represents a collection of related families?
questions.explanation: Order is a taxonomic category that groups related families together.

questions.question:
Statement I: Increase in mass and number are twin characteristics of growth.
Statement II: In plants, growth by cell division occurs continuously throughout life.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct - growth involves mass increase, and in plants, growth continues throughout life.

questions.question:
Statement I: Reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic.
Statement II: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are living and show metabolism.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct - reproduction cannot define all living things. Statement II is incorrect - isolated reactions are not living.

questions.question:
Statement I: As we go higher from species to kingdom, common characteristics increase.
Statement II: Lower taxa share more characteristics.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect - characteristics decrease from species to kingdom. Statement II is correct - lower taxa share more characteristics.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Non-living objects also grow if increase in mass is taken as a criterion.
Reason (R): Mass increases in non-living objects by accumulation of material.
options: Both A and R are true, R is correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT correct explanation
A is true, R is false
Both A and R are false
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason correctly explains why non-living objects can grow by accumulation.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Scientific names are printed in italics.
Reason (R): Italics indicate their Latin origin.
options: Both A and R are true, R is correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT correct explanation
A is true, R is false
Both A and R are false
questions.explanation: Both statements are true - scientific names are printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Systematics takes into account evolutionary relationships.
Reason (R): Word systematics comes from Latin word 'systema'.
options: Both A and R are true, R is correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT correct explanation
A is true, R is false
Both A and R are false
questions.explanation: Both are true but the reason doesn't correctly explain why systematics includes evolutionary relationships.

questions.question:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Man (B) Housefly (C) Mango (D) Wheat
Column-II: (1) Sapindales (2) Poales (3) Primata (4) Diptera
questions.explanation: Man(Primata), Housefly(Diptera), Mango(Sapindales), Wheat(Poales)

questions.question:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Family (B) Kingdom (C) Species (D) Genus
Column-II: (1) Highest category (2) Basic unit (3) Related species (4) Related families
questions.explanation: Family(Related families), Kingdom(Highest), Species(Basic unit), Genus(Related species)

questions.question:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Mango (B) Wheat (C) Housefly (D) Man
Column-II: (1) Muscidae (2) Hominidae (3) Anacardiaceae (4) Poaceae
questions.explanation: Mango(Anacardiaceae), Wheat(Poaceae), Housefly(Muscidae), Man(Hominidae)

questions.question: Which of the following represents ascending order of hierarchy?
options: Species -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum/Division -> Kingdom
Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species
Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species -> Class -> Phylum -> Kingdom
Genus -> Species -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum -> Kingdom
questions.explanation: The correct ascending order from smallest to largest is Species -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum -> Kingdom.

questions.question: Growth in unicellular organisms can be observed in vitro by:
options: Counting the number of cells under microscope
questions.explanation: Growth in unicellular organisms like Amoeba is observed by counting cell numbers, as growth is synonymous with reproduction.

questions.question: Growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events in:
options: Majority of higher animals and plants
questions.explanation: In most higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are separate processes that don't occur simultaneously.

questions.question: For unicellular organisms like Amoeba, growth is synonymous with:
questions.explanation: In unicellular organisms, growth (increase in cell number) and reproduction (cell division) are the same process.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms multiply by fragmentation?
options: Fungi, filamentous algae, protonema of mosses
questions.explanation: Fragmentation is a mode of reproduction in fungi, filamentous algae, and protonema of mosses.

questions.question: True regeneration is observed in which of the following organisms?
questions.explanation: Planaria exhibits true regeneration where a lost body part can develop into a complete organism.

questions.question: Which pair of organisms is non-reproducing?
questions.explanation: Mules and sterile worker bees are examples of non-reproducing organisms, yet they are living.

questions.question: Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems. These isolated reactions are:
questions.explanation: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are non-living because they lack cellular organization and organization.

questions.question: The defining property of living organisms among the following is:
questions.explanation: All three - cellular organization, intrinsic growth, and consciousness are defining properties of living organisms.

questions.question: What is the approximate estimated number of species known and described on Earth?
questions.explanation: Approximately 1.7 to 1.8 million species have been known and described on Earth.

questions.question: ICBN stands for:
questions.explanation: ICBN is the International Code for Botanical Nomenclature used for naming plants.

questions.question: ICZN stands for:
questions.explanation: ICZN is the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature used for naming animals.

questions.question: Binomial Nomenclature was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Carolous Linnaeus introduced the binomial system of nomenclature in the 18th century.

questions.question: In a biological name, the first word represents ____ and the second component is ____.
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first word is the genus name and the second is the species epithet.

questions.question: When handwritten, scientific names are:
questions.explanation: When handwritten, scientific names are underlined to represent italics in printed form.

questions.question: Taxonomy involves four basic processes. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: The four processes of taxonomy are characterisation, identification, nomenclature, and classification. Evolution is related but not a basic process.

questions.question: Which term includes characterisation, identification, nomenclature, classification, AND evolutionary relationships?
questions.explanation: Systematics is the broader term that includes all these aspects including evolutionary relationships.

questions.question: Taxonomic category is a part of overall taxonomic arrangement called:
questions.explanation: The taxonomic hierarchy is the step-wise arrangement of all taxonomic categories.

questions.question: Each unit of classification is commonly termed as:
questions.explanation: Each unit of classification at any level is called a taxon.

questions.question: Plural form of taxon is:
questions.explanation: Plural of taxon is taxa.

questions.question: Which of the following is the basic, lowest unit in taxonomic hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Species is the basic and lowest unit in taxonomic hierarchy.

questions.question: Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Solanum nigrum share which common taxonomic rank?
questions.explanation: Both share the genus Solanum but have different species epithets (tuberosum and nigrum).

questions.question: Panthera leo (lion), Panthera pardus (leopard), and Panthera tigris (tiger) belong to genus:
questions.explanation: All three big cats belong to genus Panthera.

questions.question: Cats belong to the genus:
questions.explanation: Cats are placed under genus Felis.

questions.question: Genus comprises a group of related:
questions.explanation: Genus comprises a group of related species.

questions.question: Plant families like Solanaceae and Convolvulaceae are included in order Polymoniales mainly based on:
questions.explanation: Plant families are grouped into orders mainly based on floral characters.

questions.question: Order Carnivora includes families like:
questions.explanation: Order Carnivora includes families Felidae (cats) and Canidae (dogs).

questions.question: Class Mammalia includes order Primata along with order:
questions.explanation: Class Mammalia includes orders Primata and Carnivora among others.

questions.question: Plants belonging to different classes with common characters like flowers and seeds are assigned to:
questions.explanation: Plants with flowers and seeds are assigned to Division Angiospermae.

questions.question: In animal taxonomy, classes having dorsal hollow neural system and notochord are placed under Phylum:
questions.explanation: Animals with dorsal hollow nerve cord and notochord belong to Phylum Chordata.

questions.question: Which of the following scientific names belongs to human beings?
questions.explanation: Homo sapiens is the scientific name for humans.

questions.question: Housefly belongs to which Phylum?
questions.explanation: Housefly (Musca domestica) belongs to Phylum Arthropoda.

questions.question: Wheat belongs to Class:
questions.explanation: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) belongs to Class Monocotyledonae.

questions.question: Mango belongs to Class:
questions.explanation: Mango (Mangifera indica) belongs to Class Dicotyledonae.

questions.question: Ernst Mayr is widely known as the:
questions.explanation: Ernst Mayr is known as the Darwin of the 20th century for his work on evolution.

questions.question: Ernst Mayr was awarded which three prestigious prizes (The Balzan Prize, International Prize for Biology, Crafoord Prize) collectively called:
questions.explanation: The Balzan Prize, International Prize for Biology, and Crafoord Prize together form the Triple Crown of Biology.
